metadata.title: Western Blot - Thermo Fisher Chemiluminescent Transfer and Detection
metadata.purpose: SDS-PAGE to membrane transfer, blocking, primary/secondary antibody incubation, HRP chemiluminescent detection.
metadata.scope: Thermo Fisher Scientific western blot protocols and recipes. SDS-PAGE to membrane transfer, blocking, primary/secondary antibody incubation, HRP chemiluminescent detection.
beforeYouBegin: Choose membrane: PVDF often for hydrophobic/stripping needs; nitrocellulose for low background/ease. Activate PVDF in alcohol before equilibration.
Match transfer buffer and method to gel chemistry, protein size, and transfer apparatus.
Plan antibody dilutions empirically and include positive, negative, and loading controls.
Avoid sodium azide with HRP-labeled antibodies.

materials.specification: Optional, for total protein transfer documentation

tables.title: Troubleshooting
rows: Transfer failure, antibody mismatch, inactive substrate.

steps.action: After SDS-PAGE, equilibrate gel in transfer buffer if required.
Prepare membrane. Wet PVDF in methanol or ethanol briefly, rinse in water, then equilibrate in transfer buffer; equilibrate nitrocellulose directly in transfer buffer.
Assemble transfer stack in correct orientation with no trapped bubbles.
steps.criticalNotes: Confirm electrode orientation before starting electrophoresis or transfer. DNA/RNA generally migrates toward the positive electrode; SDS-coated proteins migrate toward the anode.

steps.action: Run wet, semi-dry, or dry transfer according to the selected Thermo apparatus instructions.
After transfer, rinse membrane and optionally document total protein transfer with reversible stain.
steps.expectedResult: Prestained marker should transfer and be visible in expected orientation.

steps.action: Block membrane for 30-60 minutes at room temperature with agitation.
Dilute primary antibody in appropriate blocking or wash buffer and incubate 1 hour at room temperature or overnight at 2-8 deg C.

parameters.rawText: 1 hour at room temperature or overnight at 2-8 deg C

steps.action: Wash membrane 3 times for about 10 minutes each in wash buffer.

repeat.notes: About 10 minutes each in wash buffer

steps.action: Incubate with HRP-conjugated secondary antibody for about 1 hour at room temperature with agitation.
Wash thoroughly, commonly multiple short washes, to reduce unbound secondary antibody.
Prepare chemiluminescent substrate working solution and incubate membrane for the substrate-specific time.
Drain excess substrate, protect blot in clear wrap/sheet, remove bubbles, and image using film or digital imager.
steps.expectedResult: Target protein bands visible at expected molecular weight.

safety: Wear lab coat, gloves, and eye protection. Treat gels, membranes, stains, acrylamide, methanol, formaldehyde, UV exposure, and radioactive/nonradioactive probes according to local EHS rules.
Use a fume hood for formaldehyde, methanol, chloroform-like solvents, powdered stains, and hazardous probe/detection reagents when required.
Acrylamide monomer is neurotoxic before polymerization. Use appropriate PPE and dispose of unpolymerized acrylamide waste correctly.
Confirm electrode orientation before starting electrophoresis or transfer. DNA/RNA generally migrates toward the positive electrode; SDS-coated proteins migrate toward the anode.
Record gel percentage, buffer system, voltage/current, run time, stain/probe/antibody details, membrane type, exposure, image file, and deviations.
